about: Homework for this pillar, one list per AI (Claude writes it; tools/kit/render.py in jpavia10/prometheus-hub turns it into docs/agents/QUEUE_{ai}.md and the Drive docs). Every task says exactly what to read, what to make, how many, where to save it, how Claude checks it and what makes it not done. A task is done only when the file passes the checks, never because it was sent.

tasks.title: Atlas: the Federal Reserve bank holidays 2026 to 2030, as observed (55 rows) to check the payday arithmetic
tasks.why: Atlas moves a payday that falls on a bank holiday to the business day before (pillars/atlas/pay.js). Its holiday list is computed; it needs an outside list to be checked against.
tasks.unlocks: A unit test that compares Atlas's holidays with the Federal Reserve's own list for five years.
inputs: pillars/atlas/pay.js in jpavia10/prometheus-hub (the rules it uses, top of the file)
steps: For each year 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029 and 2030, list the 11 holidays on the Federal Reserve's schedule.
Give the calendar date and the date the Federal Reserve is closed (a Sunday holiday is observed on the Monday; a Saturday one is not moved).
Where the schedule for a year is not published yet, take the rule from the page that states it and say so in the note.

deliver.shape: JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below

fields.name: holiday
fields.rule: its name on the schedule

fields.name: date
fields.rule: the calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD

fields.name: closed
fields.rule: the day the Federal Reserve is closed for it, or none for a Saturday

fields.name: note
fields.rule: empty, or why

fields.name: source_url
fields.rule: the official page that shows the value (a .gov, the statute, or the agency's own page)

fields.name: checked
fields.rule: the day you read it, YYYY-MM-DD

tasks.done_when: 55 rows, 11 a year for five years.
checks: Claude runs every row through ATLAS_PAY.holidays() and every difference is either a fix to pay.js or a rejected row.
rejected_if: a value without a source URL that shows it
rows missing to reach the count
a source that is a blog, forum, law-firm marketing page or AI summary where an official page exists
a value for a year that has not been published yet presented as if it had (write "not published as of {date}" instead)

tasks.title: Atlas: the 2026 and 2027 payroll numbers for a California employee (wage bases, rates, plan limits) with their official pages
tasks.why: Atlas checks each pay stub's withholding. The rates and caps change every year: Social Security's wage base, Medicare's extra 0.9 % threshold, California SDI's rate and wage base, the 401(k), HSA and FSA limits.
tasks.unlocks: Atlas can say when a stub's Social Security stops (the wage base is reached) and what the year's plan limits are.
inputs: https://www.irs.gov (the 401(k), HSA, FSA and Medicare pages)
https://edd.ca.gov (the SDI rate and taxable wage limit page)
steps: For each year 2026 and 2027 give: Social Security tax rate and wage base; Medicare rate; Additional Medicare tax rate and its thresholds (single, joint); California SDI rate and taxable wage limit; 401(k) elective deferral limit and the age-50 catch-up; the age 60 to 63 catch-up; HSA self-only and family limits; health FSA limit.
One row per number. A 2027 number not yet published: say so in the note, value empty.

deliver.shape: JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below

fields.name: item
fields.rule: what it is, as named above

fields.name: value
fields.rule: a rate as a decimal (0.062), dollars as a number

fields.name: note
fields.rule: empty, or not published / the condition

fields.name: source_url
fields.rule: the official page that shows the value (a .gov, the statute, or the agency's own page)

fields.name: checked
fields.rule: the day you read it, YYYY-MM-DD

checks: Claude opens every source URL and checks the value.
rejected_if: a value without a source URL that shows it
rows missing to reach the count
a source that is a blog, forum, law-firm marketing page or AI summary where an official page exists
a value for a year that has not been published yet presented as if it had (write "not published as of {date}" instead)

tasks.title: Atlas: California pay rules that touch a paycheck and time off (Labor Code), with the statute for each
tasks.why: Atlas tells Joseph when a stub or a time-off balance looks wrong. In California a vacation cap is allowed but forfeiting earned vacation is not, a stub must show set items, and paydays have legal deadlines.
tasks.unlocks: Atlas's stub check can list what a California stub must show, and its time-off panel can say what happens to vacation at a cap and when leaving a job.
inputs: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/ (the DLSE's own FAQ pages on vacation, paydays and pay stubs)
steps: One row per rule: the paydays a month and how soon after the pay period wages are due (204); final pay when fired and when quitting (201, 202) and the waiting-time penalty (203); each item a pay stub must show (226), one row per item; vacation: no forfeiture, caps allowed, paid out at the end (227.3 and the DLSE vacation FAQ); paid sick leave: how much and how it accrues (246, as amended).

deliver.shape: JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below

fields.name: topic
fields.rule: paydays, final pay, pay stub, vacation or sick leave

fields.name: rule
fields.rule: the rule in one plain sentence

fields.name: section
fields.rule: Labor Code section

fields.name: quote
fields.rule: the words of the statute or the DLSE page that say it, copied exactly

fields.name: source_url
fields.rule: the official page that shows the value (a .gov, the statute, or the agency's own page)

fields.name: checked
fields.rule: the day you read it, YYYY-MM-DD

tasks.done_when: At least 20 rows covering all five topics, every pay-stub item one row.
checks: Claude opens ten source URLs at random and finds each quote on the page.
rejected_if: a value without a source URL that shows it
rows missing to reach the count
a source that is a blog, forum, law-firm marketing page or AI summary where an official page exists
a value for a year that has not been published yet presented as if it had (write "not published as of {date}" instead)
a quote that is not on the page word for word

tasks.title: Atlas: an employee's 2027 tax calendar (federal and California)
tasks.why: Atlas tracks paydays and pay stubs; the dates that matter around them (W-2 deadline, estimated tax dates, new withholding tables) belong on the same calendar.
tasks.unlocks: Atlas publishes these dates to the hub's deadline bus.
steps: Every 2027 date an employee in California may need: W-2 by, estimated tax payments (federal and FTB), filing deadline, extension deadline, IRA contribution deadline, new withholding tables in force.
Where a 2027 date is not published, give the rule and say so.

deliver.shape: JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below

fields.name: n
fields.rule: row

fields.name: what
fields.rule: the deadline

fields.name: date
fields.rule: YYYY-MM-DD

fields.name: who
fields.rule: IRS, FTB or EDD

fields.name: source_url
fields.rule: the page that shows the value

fields.name: quote
fields.rule: under 300 characters, word for word

fields.name: checked
fields.rule: the day you read it, YYYY-MM-DD

self_check: Every row has a URL you opened yourself today, on the agency's, maker's or archive's own site.
Every quote is copied word for word from that page and is there now.
The file is valid JSON and is named exactly as asked.
checks: Claude checks the dates against the IRS and FTB calendars.
rejected_if: a value without a source URL that shows it
a quote that is not word for word on the page as served today
a source that is a blog, forum, law-firm marketing page, reseller or AI summary where an official page exists
rows missing to reach the count, or rows padded to reach it
a value for a period not published yet presented as if it were (write "not published as of {date}")

tasks.title: Atlas: second reader on Gemini's California pay rules
tasks.why: Nothing Gemini delivers is built on until a second reader has checked it.
tasks.unlocks: Claude builds from the file only after this check.
inputs: Gemini's file atlas_gemini_ca-pay-rules_*.json in the folder below (ATL-GEM-03)
steps: Open Gemini's file. Pick 12 rows at random (every row if fewer).
For each, open its source URL and compare every field with the page: agree, or what the page says instead.
Add up to 5 rows Gemini missed, in Gemini's exact shape.

deliver.shape: markdown table: row | Gemini says | what I found | URL | agree/differ, then the list of what is missing

fields.name: agree/differ
fields.rule: differ needs what you found and where

checks: Claude re-reads three of your 'differ' rows against the page.
rejected_if: a verdict without the page it came from
